title: Deep Hedging with Options Using the Implied Volatility Surface

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors propose a deep reinforcement learning framework for managing index option portfolios by jointly modeling S&P 500 returns and the full implied volatility surface using the JIVR model. The agent's policy function, parameterized by a recurrent neural network (RNN-FNN), takes an enriched state vector containing implied volatility surface factors and portfolio/option Greeks to determine optimal daily rebalancing in the underlying asset and a longer-maturity hedging option. A soft constraint is incorporated into the objective function to penalize excessive risk-taking and prevent speculative behavior.
extraction.universe: S&P 500 index options and underlying asset, tested on historical European straddles

key_findings: Deep hedging agents utilizing information from the full implied volatility surface consistently outperform traditional delta and delta-gamma hedging strategies across various market conditions.
Incorporating a longer-maturity option as an additional hedging instrument significantly reduces terminal hedging error and variance when combined with deep reinforcement learning.
RL agents naturally adopt smaller initial hedging option positions and scale up gradually, which avoids large transaction costs and minimizes short exposure to the variance risk premium.

Out-of-sample backtesting on actual historical option data from 2020 to 2023 demonstrates that RL strategies maintain robust performance and superior downside risk control compared to benchmark models.
limitations: The market simulator relies on estimated joint dynamics which may be subject to specification errors.
Training requires extensive simulated paths and hyperparameter tuning (such as the soft constraint penalty weight).
